ct_porcupine_wall.blurb: A compact cliff on Rattlesnake Mountain in central Connecticut, mostly traditional lines with a handful of top-rope-only options and a few boulder problems at its base. The 22 climbs spread from very easy terrain up through the 5.10s and into the low 5.11 range, with the bulk in the easier and middle grades, so it suits a mixed party. It is the nearest of the cliffs along the ridge trail, though still a longer walk than some neighbours, and it tends to stay shaded, which helps on warm days. Pair it with the other walls further down the same trail for a fuller day.
ct_porcupine_wall.parking_note: Leave the car in the pull-off on the left side of Route 6 (Colt Highway) near the Rattlesnake Mountain trail access; a short connector leads to the blue-blazed ridge trail.
ct_porcupine_wall.approach: From the lot, take the short connector to the blue-blazed ridge trail and head south. This is the first cliff reached along that trail, before the other walls further along. The start of the path can be muddy.

ct_dark_hollow.blurb: A bouldering tract in the woods of southeastern Connecticut, part of the Mystic-area collection of boulder zones. It holds 22 problems, all of them boulders, ranging from easy V1 up through a cluster of V5 to V7 lines and a few at V10 and beyond. The headline feature is a very steep cave near the entrance, which draws the harder climbers; the remainder of the tract is more moderate with plenty of mid-grade options. Trails between the boulders are shared with off-road vehicles, so expect a rough, lived-in feel. Bring pads for uneven ground and plan on a modest hike between blocks.

ct_judges_cave.blurb: A bouldering zone on the traprock ridge of West Rock in New Haven, around 590 feet up. Its 21 problems are almost all boulders, sitting mainly in the V0 to V4 range with a single harder line near V6, which makes it a friendly place for newer boulderers and anyone wanting volume. Landings are described as good, the rock is solid, and many of the standard lines have extra variations to play on. In the colder months the walk in from the car takes around a quarter of an hour; in warmer months the approach is shorter.

ct_frankenrock.blurb: A single large traprock boulder in a wooded neighbourhood preserve in Woodbridge, just outside New Haven. Several faces offer climbing, including one steep overhanging side about 18 feet tall. The 21 problems run from a couple of very easy ones through a solid middle of V2 to V4, then climb steadily into the V7 to V10 range for strong climbers, with some harder projects left. It is a short, quick-session spot rather than a destination, and the walk in is on well-worn woodland paths of roughly half a mile.
ct_frankenrock.approach: From Park Lane, follow the blue trail for about a quarter mile, crest the hill on the right, and the boulder lies roughly another quarter mile beyond. Part of that trail has been rerouted near new houses, so a gravel drive and an unmarked trail may be needed to rejoin it.

ct_wintergreen.blurb: Boulders and bouldering walls perched above the cliffs of West Rock in New Haven, looking out over the valley below. The terrain is a mix of slabs, cliff edges and talus. Most of the 20 climbs are boulder problems, from very easy up to about V5, with many being slab problems and quite a few in the beginner range; a handful of roped trad and sport lines in the 5.7 to 5.11 range round it out. The view is a big part of the appeal, and it works well as a relaxed, low-grade outing.

ct_interstate_homeless_camp.blurb: A bouldering zone in the Westwoods forest, on the Granite Road side and tucked right beside the interstate. All 20 problems are boulders and most are easy: a good share at V0 and V1, a few at V2 and V3, and just one at V4, so it is mainly a warm-up and mileage spot. The terrain varies, with a small boulder field, short cliff-sized bands and some low cave cracks. Expect an uphill trail and a short stretch of off-trail walking to reach the rock.

fl_dames_cave.blurb: A bouldering venue in a collapsed limestone sinkhole in Citrus County, west-central Florida, part of a cluster of caves in the forest. The 23 problems run from V2 through V6, concentrated at V3 and V4, on walls about twenty feet tall. Inside the sinkhole the air stays cool and steady all year, a welcome change from Florida heat. Limestone here can be brittle, so handle the rock with care. The cave walls carry graffiti and some litter, so go prepared with pads and a sense of adventure rather than expecting a manicured crag.
fl_dames_cave.approach: An easy dirt trail of about half a mile leads from the road to the sinkhole rim; you then descend into the hole through a nearby entrance to reach the problems.
